The markers therefore emit ONLY when pre_review_check reaches status=pass with zero codes. pre_review_check currently returns exactly one code, PR_EVIDENCE_STALE, whose sole cause is these same two rows being stale. Earning them requires the markers; the markers require them earned. Everything else in the chain was repaired first and is now current: acceptance_basis_generate -> complete, acceptance_rollout_report -> signed receipt, live-smoke transcript recaptured via live_smoke_transcript --capture --write (exitCode 0), and pre_review_check went from 7 codes (PR_PRODUCTION_PATH_UNPROVEN, PR_MUTATION_EVIDENCE_MISSING, PR_MUTATION_DID_NOT_BITE, PR_CONTROL_NOT_RESTORED, PR_TRANSCRIPT_MISSING, PR_AUTHORITY_INADMISSIBLE, PR_EVIDENCE_STALE) down to 1, now reporting executableEvidence=current mutations=biting transcript=related authority=admissible. Both intents are priority=should, so no must-coverage is lost; verification.ts:188-190 isRequired() is a hard priority===must check, independently confirmed by the concept and test-coverage lanes at two separate call sites. waiverType=deferred_gate_evidence is the schema-provided mechanism for exactly this gate-self-test case and, per CLAUDE.md, does NOT count toward acceptance coverage -- so this records the gap rather than manufacturing a pass. Not fixed by widening the marker gate or the topology allow-list at :2643: that would relax a decision rule to fit our own change, which CLAUDE.md forbids. Follow-up owner should break the cycle at the source, e.g. by allowing the markers to emit when the ONLY outstanding code is PR_EVIDENCE_STALE attributable to the very intents those markers cover. Related: B-5a15:F-405 (allow-list under-enumeration) and B-5a15:F-406 (stale pre-review snapshot reuse at proofstory.ts:307-327).

commands.label: B-45a5 standing regression guard (was CHK-001's RED artifact): three clauses, all mandatory. (1) Both REVIEW-path gates must keep EXCLUDING an item-level withdrawal authorized by a confirmed decision. (2) Both must keep biting on everything that is NOT withdrawn, including an item that merely shares an authored verificationIntent id alias with a withdrawn one. (3) Both must keep REFUSING every UNBACKED withdrawal: a status flipped by hand with no decisionRef, a dangling decisionRef, a decisionRef naming a real decision that does not list the item, or a decision overwritten to decision=rejected / userConfirmed=false. Clause 3 is the safety-critical one: without it the withdrawal mechanism is forgeable by hand-editing a JSON status field. Exits 1 if any clause regresses, 2 if a control/premise breaks. CHK-003 removed the pre-fix optional flag, so this is now mandatory
